title: Lists and Indexing
content:
What problem does this solve?
One variable holding one value is not enough for an inventory, a party roster, or a queue of turns. A list stores an ordered sequence of values under a single name.

Basic syntax
  inventory = ["sword", "shield", "potion"]
  inventory[0]   # first item
  inventory.append("rope")

What actually happens
A list is a mutable object. The name inventory refers to that object. Indexing walks to a position (starting at 0). append mutates the same list object by adding another element at the end.

Why not always use separate variables? Because the number of items changes, and looping over a list scales — item1, item2, item3 does not.
concepts: append adds to the end of the same list object

examples.title: Party roster
examples.explanation: party[0] is the first name. append changes the list in place.

common_mistakes: Using index 1 when you meant the first item (that is index 0)
Confusing append (in-place) with + (which builds a new list)

exercises.title: Build an inventory
exercises.prompt:
Create a list named inventory containing the strings "sword", "shield", and "potion" in that order.
Then append "torch" and print the list.
exercises.starter_code: # Create inventory, append torch, then print
hints: Use square brackets and commas between string items.
Call inventory.append("torch") after creating the list.
